newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-WESTWOOD HITS BACK TO HOLD IRISH LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WESTWOOD HITS BACK TO HOLD IRISH LEAD.

text.p: England's Lee Westwood hit back from a poor start to increase his Irish Open lead at Druids Glen on Friday after Sweden's Michael Jonzon had blazed into contention with a course record 64, seven under par.
Westwood fell two off the lead before four back-nine birdies in six holes hauled him two clear of the field on eight-under-par 134 with Jonzon and Denmark's Thomas Bjorn in second place.
Defending champion Colin Montgomerie held fourth place a further two strokes back on 138 with Argentine Eduardo Romero on 139.
Westwood set off for his second round tied for the lead after Jonzon had beaten his day-old record by one shot.
Bjorn had posted a 70, denying himself a share of the lead with a late double-bogey.

On the tee at the long 11th, Westwood had slipped two strokes behind. Then he turned it on by hitting the green in two and taking two putts from 35 feet, followed by two approaches to only two feet for birdies and a 25-foot for another.
"I just tried to keep a level head," said Westwood. "I wasn't doing that much wrong, just causing my ball to screw back into trouble down the grain on these very grainy greens.
"I never worry anyway. My thoughts are just to hit the middle of the fairway and then play target golf and that's what I'll continue to do at the weekend.
"I've led a few times before at this stage so it's not going to be pressure for me."
Westwood is seeking to add to last year's Scandinavian Masters success and his non-Tour wins in the Taiheiyo Masters in Japan last November and the Malaysian Open this year.
He has had one second and two thirds on the European Tour this year and sits fifth on the European Ryder Cup table.
Jonzon set the record despite a bogey at the first hole. Then he ran in five successive birdies, picking up three more shots on his back nine.
"Since winning the Portuguese Open in March I've struggled," admitted Jonzon, "especially in the big events in Britain when the top European players have been on show.
"But they are all here this week and I'm glad I'm back where I was in Portugal to show that I can compete with the best."

He outshone European rankings leader Ian Woosnam, who is seven off the pace, Nick Faldo, eight behind Westwood, and Jose Maria Olazabal, 11 off the lead despite a brilliant late recovery with three birdies after looking as though he would miss his first cut since coming back from 18 months away with foot injuries.
But Sev Ballesteros shot 78 and Bernhard Langer 75 to go out of the event, well outside the four-over-par cutoff mark of 146.
